points.description: States a valid limitation of wireframe modeling: the representation is ambiguous, i.e. one wireframe model can be interpreted as several different solid objects (or it is messy/confusing to read, with no surface or solid information).
points.partial_credit: Half credit if the limitation is vague (e.g. 'not clear' or 'not accurate') without saying what is ambiguous.

points.description: Explains or qualifies the limitation using the key idea from the model answer: the same wireframe can represent different solids, or the model becomes messy and confusing because all edges are shown (no hidden lines/surfaces).
points.partial_credit: Half credit if the explanation is only partly correct or has a minor error.

rubric.notes: Full marks (2) for one limitation stating that the wireframe is ambiguous, with one model able to represent different solids, or that it is messy and confusing. Give 1 mark for a vague or half-stated limitation such as 'confusing' or 'unclear' with no reason. Give 0 for wrong or unrelated answers, such as advantages of wireframe modeling.
